- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean or recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to capture mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, reduce forecast horizon sensitivity (e.g., use 14-day moving average as anchor).
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.75), model tends to lag behind true price; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 20-day moving average), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
